state.misconception_label: Struggles to visualise nets of 3D shapes

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This is the net of a... ![A circle touching a sector](). I got Triangle because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Think of the net of a 3D shape like folding a piece of paper to make a box. Would your method still give the right answer if you were folding paper to create a shape?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Hmm, I'm not really sure... like, if I fold the paper, I don't think I'd get a triangle shape at all. But I'm confused because I see a circle and a sector thing - does that mean it folds into something round? Can you help me understand what shape actually folds from those pieces?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Imagine you were folding a piece of paper with a circle and a sector on it. Would your method still give the right answer if you were trying to create a 3D shape from those pieces?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: No, I don't think so... if I actually folded the paper, the circle and the sector would wrap around each other to make something round, not a triangle. So is it like a cone then? Because the sector would roll up and the circle would be the base?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher uses a generic folding prompt repeatedly without addressing the specific circle-sector visualization difficulty, but the student independently reasons their way to the correct cone answer through mental visualization.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses concrete, everyday analogies (folding paper, making a box) to help the student visualize the abstract concept of a net forming a 3D shape, though the repetition in Turn 3 slightly reduces the effectiveness.
